title: Multi-interpretation hub
intro: `A005251` (`0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 4, 7, 12, 21, 37, …` from `n = 0`, growth `ψ² = 1.7549`, with `ψ` the plastic number) counts six objects: the tree castles of area `n`, four more in explicit bijection with them, and the even-sector signed towers, equal in number by a change of basis ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]):
note: The gap map takes a composition of `n` to a binary string of length `n − 1`, a part `c` becoming `c − 1` zeros and the parts joined by single `1`s, and "no two adjacent parts `≥ 2`" to "no factor `010`". The complement of that string is the second row of a tower-spacing skyline of width `n − 1` with `g = 2`, which has no factor `101`. The column map sends a column of height 1 to `0` and a column of height `c ≥ 2` to `1^c`. See [[plastic-number](pages/plastic-number.md)].

title: Tree castles of area n by block parity
label: tree castles of area `n`
intro: A tree castle of area `n` and width `w` has `1 + n − w` blocks, one more than the number of zeros of its string, and by the parity of the number of blocks the tree castles of area `n` split as follows ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]). Terms from `n = 1`.
note: *(Every row agrees with enumeration for `n ≤ 20`; the OEIS has no match for the even row from `n = 2` to 13 or the odd row from `n = 1` to 13, 2026-10-25.)*

title: Castles by area with bounded height: the n-nacci family
label: castles by area
intro: A castle of area `n` is a composition of `n`, its column heights in order ([[castles-of-height-h-by-area](pages/castles-of-height-h-by-area.md)]). The castles of height at most `h` are the compositions with parts at most `h`, counted by the `h`-step Fibonacci numbers with g.f. `1/(1 − x − ⋯ − x^h)`; the castles of height 2 are the compositions into parts 1 and 2 that use a 2, `F_{n+1} − 1` of them.
note: *(Every row agrees with enumeration of compositions for `n ≤ 14` and with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-16.)*

title: Tower-spacing skylines
label: tower-spacing skylines
intro: Skylines on `{1, …, h}` in which every row `2, …, h` has its empty runs between filled cells at least `g` long, so towers that reach a row are at least `g` columns apart ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]). A column-by-column transfer matrix counts them.
note: *(A tower-spacing skyline with spacing `g` is one whose heights minus 1 are the window-`g` running minimum of some array, so the `(h, g)` count is Hardin's count of "0..(h−1) arrays, each element the minimum of `g` adjacent elements", proved on [[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]. The `h = 3` row is Hardin's table [A217883](https://oeis.org/A217883), the `h = 4` row [A217954](https://oeis.org/A217954), and the `g = 3` column [A228461](https://oeis.org/A228461). Every cell agrees with the OEIS data at the stated offset for `w ≤ 24`, and its minimal recurrence order, found by Berlekamp-Massey on 90 terms, is `(h − 1)g + 1`, 2026-10-16.)*\nThe `h = 2` row, `A005251`, `A005252`, `A005253`, `A005689` and `A098574`, has the closed form `Sum_k C(w+g−(g−1)k, 2k)` ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]).

title: The Pell castle strip: 1-smooth strips on {1, 2, 3}
label: 1-smooth strips on {1, 2, 3}
intro: Skylines on `{1, 2, 3}` whose neighboring heights differ by at most 1 ([[pell-castle-strip](pages/pell-castle-strip.md)]); the condition on the end columns picks the sequence.
note: *(Every row agrees with a transfer-matrix count for `w ≤ 24`, and every A-number row with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-16.)*

title: 1-smooth castles of height h
label: 1-smooth castles
intro: The 1-smooth rule on `{1, …, h}` ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)]) extends the Pell rows to `h = 2, …, 12`. `strips(w, h)` counts the skylines on `{1, …, h}` with first column at height 1, and `smooth(w, h)` those of height `h`, with g.f. `x^h/(η_h η_{h−1})`.

title: m-smooth castles of height h
label: m-smooth castles
intro: Skylines whose neighboring columns differ by at most `m`, with first column at height 1 ([[m-smooth-castles](pages/m-smooth-castles.md)]), for `m = 2, 3, 4`. For `h ≤ m + 1` every skyline qualifies, so with the first column at height 1 the castles of width `w ≥ 2` and height `h` number `h^{w−1} − (h−1)^{w−1}`; with any first column they number `A(w, h) = h^w − (h−1)^w`, with even-block part `A^e(w, h)`.
note: *(Every row agrees with a transfer-matrix count for `w ≤ 24`, 2026-10-16.)*

title: Motzkin castles
intro: A **Motzkin-path castle** is a 1-smooth skyline (`|c_{i+1} − c_i| ≤ 1`) with both end columns at height 1 ([[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]). Its heights minus 1 form a Motzkin path of length `w − 1`, and its block count is `1 + #up-steps`, so the even-block castles are the Motzkin paths with an odd number of up-steps.
note: *(Every row agrees with a transfer-matrix count for `w ≤ 24` or with enumeration for `s ≤ 16`, and every A-number row with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-16. All castles by semi-perimeter, `A082582`, are cornerless Motzkin paths and are equinumerous with skew Motzkin paths; they are in the section *Castles by semi-perimeter*. Their first five terms `1, 2, 5, 13, 35` agree with `A005773`, and the sixth differs, 97 against 96.)*

title: Zig-zag strips and zig-zag castles
label: zig-zag
intro: Skylines whose neighboring columns differ by exactly 1, the 1-smooth and plateau-free rules imposed together, with transfer matrix `A_path` ([[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]). `zstrips(w, h) = 𝟙ᵀ A_path^{w−1} 𝟙` counts the zig-zag strips on `{1, …, h}`, which the OEIS counts as zig-zag paths in a rectangle of width `h`, and `A_zigzag(w, h) = zstrips(w, h) − zstrips(w, h − 1)` the zig-zag castles of height `h`, in bijection with the `(h − 1)`-balanced strings of length `w − 1`. The color of a zig-zag path is the parity of its first column `c_1`.
note: *(Every row agrees with `bin/python/zig_zag_castles.py` and with every term of the OEIS data field at the stated offset, 2026-10-27.)*

title: Mersenne castles
label: Mersenne
intro: Castles whose neighboring columns, read as strings whose lengths are the column heights, sound a perfect consonance: heights in ratio 1, 2, 3/2 or 4/3, or the inverse ([[mersenne-castles](pages/mersenne-castles.md)]). `A_Mersenne(w, h)` counts the Mersenne castles of width `w` and height `h`. A consonance keeps the part of a height prime to 6, so `A_Mersenne(w, h) = A_Mersenne(w, h₀)` for `h₀` the largest divisor of `h` of the form `2^a 3^b`, and the rows are at those heights.
note: *(Every row agrees with `bin/python/mersenne_castles.py` and, where it has an A-number, with every term of the OEIS data field at the stated offset, 2026-10-28.)*

title: Ridge strips and ridge castles
intro: The ridge rule: neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height `h`, with transfer matrix `R_h = J − D` ([[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)], [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)]). The ridge strips are the skylines on `{1, …, h}` under the rule, and the ridge castles those of height `h`, `𝟙ᵀR_h^{w−1}𝟙 − (h−1)(h−2)^{w−1}` of them; their even-block part is on [[proper-castle-projection](pages/proper-castle-projection.md)].
note: *(Every row agrees with a transfer-matrix count for `w ≤ 24`, 2026-10-16.)*

title: Signed tower count P(k, ·) rows
label: signed tower count
intro: The signed tower count `P(k, L) = Σ (−1)^{blocks}` in the base length `L` at fixed tower height `k` ([[signed-tower-count](pages/signed-tower-count.md)]), with a linear recurrence of order `k + 1`. The even-`k` rows are positive (checked `k ≤ 12`, `L < 40`); for odd `k` the roots of largest modulus are a complex-conjugate pair and the rows change sign in runs.
note: *(The characteristic polynomials `char_k` are irreducible for odd `k ≤ 31`, each proved by a prime mod which it stays irreducible ([[castle-cryptography-number-theory](pages/castle-cryptography-number-theory.md)]), and have two irreducible factors for even `k ≤ 14` (computed). The denominators have the closed form `den_k = A·r_+^k + B·r_−^k` with `r_± = −x ± √(x²+1)`, on [[generating-function-gallery](pages/generating-function-gallery.md)].)*

title: Strip Perron-root sequences
label: strips
intro: Width counts of the 0/1 transfer-matrix strips of [[reachable-field-census](pages/reachable-field-census.md)] and [[metallic-strip-realizability](pages/metallic-strip-realizability.md)].
note: The quadratic strips off the line `p₂ = 1` reach the fields `Q(√17)`, `Q(√21)`, `Q(√6)`, `Q(√7)` and `Q(√33)`, each through several strip matrices, so a field has no single count sequence.

title: Castles of width w and height h
intro: The castles of width `w` and height `h`, `A(w, h) = h^w − (h−1)^w` of them, and their even-block and odd-block parts `A^e(w, h)` and `A^o(w, h)` ([[castle-notation](pages/castle-notation.md)], [[castle-counting-formula](pages/castle-counting-formula.md)]). Terms by width from `w = 1` unless stated.
note: *(The `A(w, h)` rows and the convex row agree with brute-force enumeration for `w ≤ 7` and with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-27.)*

title: Towers by number of blocks
label: towers
intro: The towers on a base of length `w` counted by their number of blocks `b` ([[tower-narayana-polynomial](pages/tower-narayana-polynomial.md)]).

title: Tree skylines and tree castles by width
intro: Tree skylines have no `2 × 2` square of cells; the tree castles of height `h` are the tree skylines that reach `h` ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]).

title: Castles by semi-perimeter
label: castles by semi-perimeter
intro: A castle's semi-perimeter is `s = w + blocks` ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)]), so these are the castle counts in Delest-Viennot's perimeter grading, with the Project Euler parity split. The g.f. are algebraic, and rational for the convex castles.
note: *(Every row agrees with enumeration for `s ≤ 16` and with the series of its g.f., and every A-number row with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-16; [[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)] checks the series through `s = 30`.)*

title: Prime castles by area
intro: Gluing castles at a shared column of height 1 makes a free monoid; its primes correspond to the castles with no column of height 1, the prime castles, `F_{n−1}` of them of area `n` ([[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]). A convex castle has at most one prime factor ([[prime-convex-castles](pages/prime-convex-castles.md)]). Terms from `n = 2` unless stated.
note: *(A peak is a maximal run of columns of height at least 2. Every row agrees with enumeration of compositions for `n ≤ 15`, 2026-10-16.)*

title: Classical polyomino families among castles, by area
label: castles by area
intro: The classical polyomino families intersected with the castles ([[castle-add-a-column-equation](pages/castle-add-a-column-equation.md)]): a monotone castle is a Ferrers or reverse-Ferrers skyline. Terms from `n = 1`.
note: *(Every row and formula agrees with enumeration of compositions for `n ≤ 15`, 2026-10-16.)*

title: Odd-block counts, parity-refined area, and joint block tables
intro: The odd-block, parity-refined and joint block rows; full terms on [[odd-castles-and-block-tables](pages/odd-castles-and-block-tables.md)].
note: *(The `h = 3` rows and the rows by area agree with enumeration for `w ≤ 8` and `n ≤ 15`, 2026-10-16.)*

title: Half-sum rows
label: half-sum
intro: The binomial half-sum of `A^e(w, h)` in the width ([[half-sum-castles](pages/half-sum-castles.md)]), `K_h(w) = Σ_k C(2k, k) A^e(w − k, h)`, with g.f. `G_h(x)/√(1 − 4x)`. Terms from the first nonzero width.

title: Tree castles by area at fixed height
label: tree castles by area
intro: Tree castles, the castles with no `2 × 2` square, of height 2 and of height at most `h ≥ 3`, by area `n` ([[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)]). For `h ≥ 3` the count at area `n` is the number of compositions of `n + 1` into parts `{1, 3, 4, …, h + 1}`; at height 2 it is the number of compositions of `n + 1` into parts `{1, 3}` that use a 3. Terms from `n = 1`. Without a bound on the height the count is `A005251(n+2)` (section *Multi-interpretation hub*).
note: *(Every row agrees with enumeration for `n ≤ 15` and with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-16.)*

title: Sandpile groups
label: sandpile groups of castles
intro: The sandpile groups of the castles with at most 16 cells, mirror images identified, in both models: `K_sink`, with one cell as the sink, and `K_tide`, with the bottom row as the sink ([[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)]). Terms by number of cells from `n = 1`.
note: *(Every row agrees with Smith normal forms of the reduced Laplacians of all castles with at most 16 cells, in both models, 2026-10-16.)*

title: Fibonacci castle sub-families
label: Fibonacci castles
intro: Fibonacci castles, the castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2, selected by a rule on their towers; terms by width from `w = 1` ([[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)]).
note: *(A tower is `(d, k)`-run-length-limited when the runs of 0s between consecutive 1s have length at least `d` and every run of 0s, the end runs included, has length at most `k`. Every row agrees with enumeration of the towers for `w ≤ 14`, 2026-10-16.)*
